title: The independent and joint effects of outdoor air pollution exposure and genetic risk on mental health trajectories during adolescence.
abstract: Longitudinal data from n=10,620 ABCD Study participants were used to test sex-stratified associations of PM2.5 exposure and polygenic risk with mental health trajectories across ages 9-16. PM2.5 was associated with smaller decreases in psychotic-like experiences over time in females. Higher PRS-SCZ and PRS-MDD were linked to greater increases in internalising symptoms in females. In females an interaction between PM2.5 and PRS-MDD on PLE trajectories was observed.
